//repos_note: The repos to discover candidate PRs in. Blank until you configure it: agent-code-review repos add <owner/name> [--unlisted <group>]. allowed_authors_only_repos is the pre-groups way to say "only discover rostered authors here"; it still works, and authors.unlisted supersedes it.
//authors_note: Author groups. An author belongs to ONE group per repo, and the group is a complete review policy: what we may do with their PRs (ignore = never discovered, though a manual queue add still reviews; comment = reviewed but never approved; approve = approvable when the review warrants it), which engine reviews them, and what extra instruction the agent gets. WHO is in each group lives in the DuckDB store, per repo, because it churns: agent-code-review authors set <owner/repo|*> <github-handle> <group>. The groups themselves live here, next to the prompts they carry. approver / commenter / ignored exist without being declared; declaring one of those names replaces it. Resolution: the author's roster row (a repo-specific row beats a '*' row), else authors.unlisted for this repo, else authors.unlisted['*']. Then every matching override patches it field by field, where empty inherits and prompts accumulate. Run `agent-code-review authors who <handle> --repo <owner/name>` to see which layer decided what.
//candidates_note: rereview_cooldown holds a PR after one of our own reviews before it can be re-discovered; quiet_period holds a PR until it has gone untouched that long (no pushes or edits); steering_hold defers a PR while its author has the steering editor open, renewed while they type and capped so an editor left open cannot park it indefinitely. Holds are named and independent: a PR is eligible once every hold on it has expired, it keeps its queue position while held, and promotion or a manual add lifts them all. '0s' disables a hold.
//schedule_note: Two independent loops, each with its own switch: discovery scrapes repos for candidates on its own poll (deterministic gh calls, no LLM); schedule consumes the queue (engine invocations, hence max_parallel). Reviews are dispatched one at a time as slots free, waiting dispatch_cooldown between hand-offs; interval is only the idle poll for when nothing is ready, and bounds how long a `queue add` from another process waits to be noticed.

schedule.//usage_floor_note: Hold a candidate when the engine that would review it has less than this % remaining in its 5h or weekly window; it runs when that window refills. Applied PER ENGINE, since a group can name its own: codex being out of headroom does not hold candidates bound for claude. A held candidate is never claimed or recorded, exactly like a cooldown hold. 0 disables a floor. Omit for the default of 10.

review.//engine_note: The DEFAULT agent CLI for reviews: "codex" or "claude". An author group can name its own engine/model/effort, which overrides this for that cohort's PRs, so one cycle can run both. Both report through the same verdict contract and write the same agent.log, so switching is a one-key change; only the matching engine block below applies, patched by whatever the resolved group asked for.
review.//main_prompt_note: The tool assumes only the gh CLI plus whichever engine CLI you selected. Your prompt may direct the agent to use anything else you have set up (skills such as pr-issue-review, extra CLIs such as agent-* tools); that is your prompt's business, and you grant any extra access via codex.args / claude.allowed_tools.
review.main_prompt: Act as a friendly PR unblocker. Review this pull request thoroughly: read the diff, the PR description, and any linked context via the gh CLI. Leave one GitHub review with inline comments that help the author move forward.
review.//post_outcome_note: on_approve / on_comment / on_reject run after the agent lands on that outcome (reject = requested changes). Put your workspace-specific conventions here (team channels, emoji rituals, notification tooling); the tool ships none of that.
review.//rules_note: Comment-only vs approval is a built-in, always-present directive (default: comment-only; approval only when the author's resolved group permits it and the PR isn't self-authored, which no group can override); you do not need a rule for it. A group's own prompt covers the unconditional case. Rules are for the conditional ones: they add EXTRA instructions when their condition matches (groups / authors / author_allowed / author_not_allowed / author_is_gh_user / candidate_type / repos). Give a rule an "outcome" (approve|comment|reject) to attach it under that post-outcome section instead of the prompt body. author_allowed now means "the resolved policy permits approval", so rules written before groups keep working. Manage rules with the 'prompts rules' command (agent-code-review prompts rules usage).
review.//resume_prompt_note: When a run ends without a final outcome (codex: an intermediate WORKING report; claude: no structured report at all), the driver resumes that session with this nudge instead of recording an ERROR. Empty uses a built-in default; the engine's max_resumes bounds the attempts.

codex.//model_note: Leave empty to use codex's own default model. To pin one, pick a valid id from `codex debug models`; an invalid id fails every review with a 400.
codex.//effort_note: Leave empty to use the selected model's default reasoning effort. To pin one, use an effort the selected model supports (today commonly low, medium, high, or xhigh).
codex.//args_note: workspace-write disables network by default, but the agent must reach GitHub via gh; this override re-enables network while keeping writes scoped to the per-PR workdir.
codex.//max_resumes_note: How many times to resume a session that ended on a WORKING report before recording an ERROR. Unset means 2; 0 disables resuming.

review.//claude_note: Applies only when engine is "claude". Requires an authenticated Claude Code CLI (`claude auth login`); the tool never handles credentials. Reviews draw on that account's subscription, and schedule.usage_floor meters it the same way it meters codex.

claude.//model_note: Defaults to claude-opus-5 when empty. Pinned rather than inherited from your account's session default, so a review's depth and cost do not change under you when that default moves. Override with an alias (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable) or a full id. NOTE: the default 'auto' permission mode requires Opus 4.6+, Sonnet 4.6+, or Fable 5; haiku and older models are unsupported there and would fail every review, so pair them with a static permission_mode.
claude.//effort_note: Defaults to medium when empty. Pinned rather than inherited from the session default, for the same reason as the model, plus one specific to this engine: a run reports no effort back, so an unpinned effort is also an unrecorded one and history could not correlate cost with effort. medium rather than the xhigh that general Opus 5 coding guidance suggests, because code review is the workload that guidance is least true of: this model holds precision and recall at lower effort. Raise this first if review quality slips. One of low, medium, high, xhigh, max.
claude.//permission_mode_note: The analogue of codex.sandbox: what the agent may do without a prompt no headless run can answer. Default 'auto' routes each action through a classifier, so the agent can use whatever tools your prompt calls for without enumerating them here; it also strips tool RESULTS before judging, so a hostile PR diff cannot talk it into approving something. The static alternatives: acceptEdits (reads + file writes + common filesystem commands, everything else needs an allowed_tools entry), dontAsk (tighter still), bypassPermissions (no checks at all; only if you trust every prompt completely).
claude.//allowed_tools_note: Pre-approved tools, in permission-rule syntax. Leave EMPTY in auto mode: allow rules resolve ahead of the classifier, so listing something here exempts it from the vetting auto mode exists to do. In the static modes an empty list falls back to the minimum a review needs (gh, plus reads).
claude.//max_budget_usd_note: Hard per-invocation ceiling (claude --max-budget-usd). On a subscription the figure is the notional API-rate valuation of the run, so this bounds a runaway review rather than literal spend. 0 means uncapped. Set it from your own data rather than guessing: every review records its cost, and the dashboard Metrics page shows the median and peak once a few have landed. A cap below your peak truncates real reviews, which is worse than no cap.
claude.//args_note: Extra args appended to `claude -p`, for anything not covered above (--mcp-config, --add-dir, --agents).
claude.//max_resumes_note: How many times to resume a session that ended without a final report before recording an ERROR. Unset means 2; 0 disables resuming.

//scoring_note: Gamifies PR authorship: every completed review earns the PR AUTHOR points. score = base x (churn / churn_unit) x size-bucket x verdict x shrink x decay^(revision-1), where churn is additions + (deletions x deletion_weight) with generated files excluded. Points scale with how much was reviewed, so the bucket multipliers set a RATE rather than a flat fee per PR: a bigger PR earns more in total but at a worse rate per line, splitting a large change into well-sized pieces earns more than shipping it whole, and fragmenting it further earns less than either. Removing code beats adding the same amount of reviewing (a removed line counts deletion_weight of an added one, and a net-negative PR earns shrink_bonus on top), and a first-pass approval beats the same approval after rounds of comments. Scores are FROZEN when a review completes alongside a hash of these rules, so retuning anything here changes what FUTURE reviews earn and leaves existing points alone; `agent-code-review score recompute` re-applies new rules to old rows and `score refetch` re-measures from GitHub. See `agent-code-review score usage`.

scoring.//mode_note: Global switch. enabled = measure each reviewed PR and score it. leaderboard-only = STOP measuring (this removes the only ongoing network cost scoring adds, one GitHub call per review) while still showing the points already earned. disabled = no scoring, and the leaderboard is hidden in the dashboard. Can be narrowed per repo under scoring.repos.
scoring.//base_note: Points for one CHURN_UNIT of lines at multiplier 1.0. Score scales with the size of the change rather than being a flat fee per PR: a flat fee is farmable without bound, because points then track how many PRs you opened rather than how much was reviewed (2,000 lines split into 200 ten-line PRs scored 1000x the same change shipped whole). With scaling, the bucket multipliers set the RATE work is paid at, so the most any decomposition can gain is the spread between the best and worst rates: 7.5x at these defaults, and you get it by landing in the small bucket.
scoring.//churn_unit_note: How many lines base pays for. 50 means base is the points for a full small-bucket PR at multiplier 1.0.
scoring.//curve_note: How a size tier's multiplier applies across its range. 'linear' (the default) reads each max_churn as an ANCHOR and moves the multiplier smoothly between them, interpolated on log(churn) because the tiers are spaced geometrically; the worst a single line can cost is 0.4% of the rate. 'step' holds one multiplier across the whole tier, which states in one line what any PR is worth at the cost of a cliff at every boundary: one line over 1000 churn costs 60% of the rate. Neither widens what splitting a change can gain, since that is best rate over worst rate and interpolation moves neither end. Repeating a multiplier on two consecutive tiers holds it flat between them, which keeps the peak a range worth aiming at rather than an exact number worth hitting.
scoring.//deletion_weight_note: How much a REMOVED line counts toward size compared with an added one. Below 1 because removed code is cheaper to read than new code, so a deletion-heavy PR lands in a smaller bucket. Together with shrink_bonus this is two expressions of the same preference; tune one at a time.
scoring.//buckets_note: Size tiers, matched in order against churn = additions + (deletions x deletion_weight), with generated files already excluded. max_churn is an INCLUSIVE upper bound; the last bucket omits it and catches everything else. Each multiplier is a RATE per churn_unit, not a flat fee, so a bigger PR still earns more in total (it is more work) but at a worse rate per line. Under the default 'linear' curve the open-ended tier's anchor is derived far enough out to keep that true: points are churn x rate, so a rate falling faster than churn rises would have made a slightly smaller PR worth more. The peak sits at the small tier: splitting a large change into well-sized pieces earns more than shipping it whole, and fragmenting it further earns less again.
scoring.//verdicts_note: Multiplier per outcome. requested_changes is negative, so a rejected round actively costs points and a leaderboard can go below zero; set it to 0 if you would rather quality pressure came only from the decay. SKIPPED and ERROR never score: they are our machinery's outcomes, not the author's work.
scoring.//shrink_bonus_note: Multiplier when a PR is net-negative overall. Only ever a bonus: it never deepens the penalty on a rejected PR.
scoring.//attempt_decay_note: Applied as decay^(revision-1), so each further round of review on the same PR is worth less. Must be under 1: at exactly 1 nothing decays and comment-comment-approve would outscore getting it right first time. Counts REVISIONS, not reviews, so replying to the bot at the same commit costs nothing.
scoring.//use_gitattributes_note: Read the repo OWN .gitattributes to leave linguist-generated and linguist-vendored files out of the size, honouring git own rules (every ancestor directory file applies, last match wins, and !attr undoes an earlier rule). This is the same declaration that collapses them in GitHub diff view, and it deliberately keeps the list of what counts as generated with each repo rather than here. A repo that has not marked its generated files will see them counted until it does. NOTE that exclusion settings are part of the RULES and are hashed with them, so changing one marks the rows scored under the old policy stale. They can be re-applied offline: each row stores its per-file measurement, so `score recompute --stale` re-decides what counts without asking GitHub again. `score refetch` is only for a row whose measurement is missing or describes a revision the review never saw.
scoring.//exclude_paths_note: Extra globs excluded from the size, for repos that have not adopted linguist-generated. Gitignore-style: 'vendor/**', '*.pb.go', 'package-lock.json'.
scoring.//repos_note: Per-repo overrides, keyed 'owner/name'. Each entry patches the settings above field by field; buckets and exclude_paths REPLACE rather than append. Example: { "owner/monorepo": { "base": 50, "exclude_paths": ["generated/**"] } }
